hypothesis: MDL over a 25-point concern-parameter grid consistently recovers the true compiler theta*=(0,0) at N=2000 paired samples with recovery rate >= 0.95 (Theorem CT-1), and the Boltzmann ecology update K_{t+1} proportional to K_t exp(beta r) is monotone non-decreasing in expected reward at every beta in {0.1, 1.0, 4.0} and converges to the fiber argmax at beta=4.0 (Theorem CT-2), on the 4-bit Boolean world of Instrument 4.

controls.description: The 5x5 concern grid contains theta*=(0,0), so MDL is not forced to pick a nearest-approximation.
All (s, x) sampling for CT-1 uses a seeded Mulberry32 PRNG; recovery rate is exact under the seed sequence.
Boltzmann update K_{t+1}(x|s) is normalised to sum 1 on every fiber; asserted in tests.
Reward monotonicity is checked at every t in 0..19 and every z in Z; failure at any one point flips the gate.

gates.criterion: MDL over the 25-point concern-parameter grid recovers theta*=(0,0) with rate >= 0.95 at N=2000 across 100 seeds.
Recovery rate is non-decreasing across N in {50, 100, 200, 500, 1000, 2000} up to 0.15 finite-seed slack.
Expected reward per fiber is non-decreasing in t across 20 Boltzmann steps at every beta in {0.1, 1.0, 4.0}.
At beta=4.0 after 20 steps, expected reward is within 0.05 of the fiber argmax on every z.
